import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 431

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/431](https://www.erdosproblems.com/431)
-/

namespace Erdos431

open scoped Pointwise

/-- Are there two infinite sets $A$ and $B$ such that $A+B$ agrees with the primes up to finitely
many exceptions? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_431 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧
      (A + B : Set ℕ) =ᶠ[Filter.cofinite] {n | n.Prime} := by
  sorry

end Erdos431

findings.description: The domain `A B : Set ℕ` permits zero in either summand, whereas the primary treatments explicitly use positive-integer summands. The cited webpage omits this domain restriction, so this is a modelling ambiguity, not an established inequivalence. Removing zero is not automatically harmless: it can remove infinitely many sums, despite the cofinite equality condition. Many zero-containing witnesses can be translated into positive ones, but a putative witness with `0 ∈ A` and `1 ∈ B` (or vice versa) cannot be handled by opposite translations. I could not establish whether this remaining case is impossible or yields an equivalent positive-summand decomposition.
findings.source_evidence: Elsholtz–Harper, arXiv:1309.0593, Definition 1.1 explicitly says “two sets of positive integers A and B, with at least two elements each” and requires `(A+B) ∩ [x₀,∞) = S ∩ [x₀,∞)`; Conjecture 1.2 applies this to the primes. Elsholtz, “The inverse Goldbach problem” (2001), §1, and Croot–Elsholtz (2005), §1, also explicitly require positive integers. In contrast, https://www.erdosproblems.com/431 merely says “two infinite sets A and B.”
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify the intended summand domain. To match the explicit positive-integer formulations, add `0 ∉ A ∧ 0 ∉ B` to the conjunction. Alternatively, retain the current domain with a reference or equivalence argument justifying nonnegative summands.

reformulations.difference: Uses eventual equality of set predicates along `Filter.cofinite` instead of explicitly requiring finitely many exceptions.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `Set.mem_add` gives the usual sumset membership condition. `Filter.eventuallyEq_set` and `Filter.eventually_cofinite` identify the exceptional set with the symmetric difference of `A+B` and the primes. Its finiteness is also equivalent, on ℕ, to the existence of N such that every n ≥ N is representable as a+b with a ∈ A and b ∈ B exactly when n is prime. Both equivalences, including the full existential formulation, were proved in the scratch file.

could_not_verify: Erdos431.erdos_431 — only the equivalence of the zero-inclusive summand domain with the explicit positive-integer formulations in the primary literature remains unsettled, as described in the questionable finding.
review.notes: No definite misformalization was established. The source still records OPEN, matching `research open`; the answer slot has the correct type, scope, and polarity. All definitions, quantifiers, conjunctions, and finite-exception semantics otherwise check out. `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` compiles without warnings or errors and contains the equivalence proofs, small sumset/primality tests, a proof excluding zero in both summands, and a general example showing that deleting zero can lose infinitely many sums. That example is not a counterexample to the prime conjecture. The target file was not modified.
